DAY 7
Lead-in · 4 min

Why is this man so fat?

Look at the photo like a detective. Find five clues in the room. Then click a cause to compare.

Clues?
🍕
What he eats
pizza, crisps, chocolate, sugary drinks – high-calorie food, big portions, snacks all day
🛋️
How he lives
sofa + TV + remote; the treadmill is a clothes hanger – almost no exercise
🧬
Things he can't choose
genes, some illnesses, some medicines, stress and poor sleep – be fair, not everything is a "choice"
💷
The world around him
cheap fast food everywhere, cars, desk jobs – in the UK and US about 1 in 4 adults is obese
Language: be overweight → be fat (informal, a bit rude) → be obese (medical). Today's text uses fat – it is a friend talking about a friend.
So what can he do? One phrase – you'll need it today.
go on a diet = start eating less / only certain foods to lose weight. He is on a diet. He broke his diet.
Skim · 2 min

Read fast. One question.

2:00
Q · the only questionHugh has been on a diet for a week. Is it working? Find two sentences that prove your answer.
No. ① "Hugh was still as fat as ever." ② "It contained five large bars of chocolate and three bags of sweets!" – he is eating the forbidden foods.

Grammar focus

"…so strict that he had to reward himself."

Cause → result. so + adjective/adverb + that + clause. With a noun: such (a) + adj + noun + that.

Result machine

Hugh wassoadjectivethatresult
so + adj / adv + thatsuch + (a) + adj + NOUN + that
so fat that… · so quickly that… · so many sweets that… / such a strict diet that… · such bad things that…
Shortcut: so/such…that → too…to / enough to (a different structure, same idea).

Wrap-up

Where is the virtue?

💬 Discuss (3 min)

"His diet was so strict that he had to reward himself occasionally."
  • Reward for virtue – what is the "virtue" here? Did Hugh show any? (Irony: he rewards himself for self-control he doesn't have.)
  • Is Hugh lying, or does he believe his own excuse? Have you ever made an excuse like this?
  • Back to the photo: what ONE small change would you suggest to Hugh – and how would you say it kindly?

📝 Homework

  • Retell in 60–80 words as Hugh ("I've always been fat, but…") – keep both so…that sentences.
  • Six sentences: three with so…that, three with such…that, about your own week.
  • Write Hugh's new list for next week – five forbidden things, five allowed things, in two columns.
Look at the picture. What do you think it means? Guess in English!
